newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.58/1.53 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.65/1.60 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.68/1.63 percent against 1.72/1.67 percent.
Among bonds, April 1998 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$99.53/99.58.
September 2001 ended at S$96.70/96.75 from Monday's S$96.69/96.74 and June 2003 at S$94.75/94.80 versus S$94.73/94.78.
The interbank rate rose to 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent against Monday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
